hints: Notice that three of these statements all describe the same trend down Group 2, so look for what they have in common.
Remember that atomic radius, reactivity with water, and hydroxide solubility all increase going down Group 2.
Spot the odd one out that names a specific familiar compound, calcium carbonate for liming, and that must belong to the metal higher up the group.
walkthrough:
**Spot the linked trends**

Think like a detective. Three statements are really saying the same thing: lower down Group 2.

Reactivity increases down the group:
$$\text{M(s) + 2H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2\text{(aq) + H}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Group the three that go together**

Greater atomic radius is clearly down the group, as extra shells are added. Faster reaction with cold water is also down the group, as ionisation is easier. Higher pH of saturated hydroxide is also down the group, because hydroxides become more soluble.

So A, C and D all describe the lower metal. Call this metal Q.

**Identify the odd one out**

The carbonate used to neutralise acidic soil in agriculture is limestone, $\text{CaCO}_3$. This is a specific identity test for calcium.

Calcium is above strontium and barium in Group 2, so it is less reactive, smaller and has a less soluble hydroxide than Q. Therefore this statement must belong to the upper metal, R.

options.A: Incorrect. Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2, so a saturated solution contains more $\text{OH}^-$ and has higher pH lower down. This describes the more reactive lower metal Q, not R.
options.B: Correct. The carbonate is $\text{CaCO}_3$, limestone, spread on fields to neutralise acid soil. This identifies R as calcium, which sits above the more reactive Q (such as Sr or Ba), so it is the odd one out.
options.C: Incorrect. Atomic radius increases down Group 2 due to additional electron shells. The greater radius therefore belongs to the lower metal Q, not R.
options.D: Incorrect. Reactivity with cold water increases down Group 2 as ionisation energy falls. The faster reaction therefore belongs to the lower metal Q, not R.
